correctness.rationale: Removing the highest-ranked good in the other bundle witnesses all the relevant prefix inequalities at once. With complete allocation, the own-count lower bound is floor(prefix length/2); odd bounds follow from the previous even bound. The market therefore forces one per pair and leaves the singleton free. An independent exhaustive replay used actual per-ranking good removals and compared sorted positions for SD dominance; it tested all 128 bundles for market feasibility, all 5040 strict orders for the resulting 16 market bundles, and checked each strict refinement within the 630 paired orders before grouping. It confirmed the full histogram, 96 exceptional paired profiles and the identical exceptional union of two disjoint 48-profile orbits generated from the reported representatives. The 64 refinements per paired profile yield 6144 failures and 8/33075. For the mean, reflection of a length-seven prefix walk at its first visit to −2 gives 35−21=14 successful three-good position sets and 35−7=28 four-good sets. Independence gives 16(14/35)(28/35)=128/25, also confirmed by the exact allocation incidence 130056192.
residual_risks: Exact only for two agents, seven completely allocated goods and strict rankings; the probability and mean require the uniform independent model.
